skills.content:
---
name: scam-email-scanner
description: >-
  Use to build, run, or maintain the inbox scam-email scanner (auth headers,
  link threat checks, scoring, spam/review actions, attachment alerts,
  dashboard, breach checks). Run when setting up the scanner or when the
  scan/dashboard/breach routines fire.
---
# Scam email scanner

All files live in `~/scam-scanner/`: `config.json`, `scan.py`, `make_dashboard.py`, `healthcheck.py`, `health.jsonl`, `breach.json`, `state.json` ({processed:[ids], last_scan}), `log.jsonl`, `raw/`, `cache/`. If any are missing, rebuild them from this spec with Python 3 stdlib only.

## config.json (written during getting-started)
`{"provider":"gmail|outlook|proton","block_threshold":90,"review_threshold":40,"flag_mode":"label|folder","flag_name":"Scam Review","alerts":"chat|email|both","alert_email":"","attachment_alerts":"all|unknown_senders|risky_types","dashboard":"chat|html|netlify (or a list)","dashboard_times":["09:00","17:00"],"scan_interval_minutes":15,"timezone":"","breach_checks":true,"virustotal_key":"","abusech_auth_key":""}`

## Providers
- **Gmail** (Gmail plugin): list new mail with `search_emails` query `in:inbox after:<last_scan>`; this excludes spam and trash by default. Fetch each message with `read_email` messageFormat RAW and save it to raw/<id>.json; RAW is the only format with Authentication-Results. The raw body may come back base64url-encoded or as plain text, so scan.py must accept both. Block with `mark_email_spam`, which moves the message and reports it. Flag by getting the label id from `list_labels`, creating the label with `create_label` if needed, then `update_email_labels` adding that label id. Tool names can change; if a call fails, re-read the connector's tool list and use the current names.
- **Outlook** (Outlook plugin): read the Inbox folder only, never Junk. Headers come from internetMessageHeaders or the MIME content. Block by moving to Junk Email (report if the tool supports it). Flag with a category, or move to a "Scam Review" folder.
- **Proton**: needs a paid plan plus Proton Mail Bridge running locally (IMAP 127.0.0.1:1143, with the Bridge password). Use IMAP `INBOX` only, `UID SEARCH SINCE`, and `BODY.PEEK[]` for raw messages. Block by moving to `Spam`. Flag by moving to the "Scam Review" folder; Proton labels show up as `Labels/...` IMAP folders.
- Everywhere: process INBOX only and never scan spam, junk, or trash. Skip ids already in state.processed.

## scan.py (input: raw messages; appends decisions to log.jsonl)
- Parse the MIME message. From (name and address), Reply-To, Subject, Date.
- Auth: regex `spf|dkim|dmarc=(\w+)` over all Authentication-Results headers, falling back to Received-SPF. Points: DMARC fail +30, SPF fail/softfail +20, DKIM fail +20, each missing +8.
- Display name contains a brand (google, apple, microsoft, paypal, amazon, discord, metamask, coinbase, binance, opensea, github, ledger, phantom, banks…) that isn't in the sender domain: +25.
- Links: HTML `<a href>` with its visible text, plus bare URLs in the text. Cache feeds for 6 hours:
  - URLhaus `https://urlhaus-api.abuse.ch/v2/files/exports/<AUTH-KEY>/recent.csv` (CSV; keep rows whose status is online). abuse.ch retired its free no-key downloads, so this needs a free Auth-Key from https://auth.abuse.ch/ (env `ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY` or `abusech_auth_key` in config.json). With no key, skip URLhaus with a warning and keep scanning with the other lists.
  - Never overwrite a cached feed with a failed, empty (<100 bytes), or HTML-error download; keep the last good copy and replace it atomically only on success.
  - OpenPhish `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openphish/public_feed/refs/heads/main/feed.txt`
  - MetaMask `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MetaMask/eth-phishing-detect/main/src/config.json` (use its blacklist and subtract its whitelist)
  - ScamSniffer `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scamsniffer/scam-database/main/blacklist/domains.json`
  - Any feed hit is +95.
  - **Shared-host rule**: for github.com, githubusercontent, google/docs/drive, dropbox, discord(cdn), microsoft/onedrive, amazonaws, cloudfront, x.com, t.co, count only an exact URL match, never a host match.
  - Heuristics: IP-literal URL +35; brand lookalike (edit distance 1, or brand-hyphen) +40; punycode +25; visible text domain different from the href domain +30; risky TLD (zip, mov, top, xyz, click, icu, tk…) +15; third-party shortener +10 (skip a shortener that belongs to the sender, e.g. t.co from x.com).
  - Domain age: query `https://rdap.org/domain/<d>` for the sender domain and up to 7 link domains, cached. Registered less than 30 days ago: +30.
  - Optional: if virustotal_key is set, GET `/api/v3/urls/<b64url id>`; 2 or more malicious detections +95.
- Urgency language (seed phrase, private key, verify wallet, claim airdrop, account suspended, gift card): +20.
- **Cap**: if DKIM and DMARC both pass and there's no feed or VirusTotal hit, cap the score at 85, so heuristics alone never auto-block. Clamp to 0–100.
- action: `spam` if score > block_threshold, `review` if score >= review_threshold, otherwise `clean`.
- Attachments: any non-multipart part with a filename or Content-Disposition attachment. Skip small (<100KB) inline images that have a Content-ID. Record attachments [{filename,type,size}] and has_attachments. Set attachment_alert per config: all; or only when the sender has never been seen in the log; or only risky types (exe, scr, js, vbs, bat, cmd, ps1, msi, iso, img, lnk, html/htm, zip/rar/7z, docm/xlsm, pdf). Attachments are never scanned.
- Log line fields: id, threadId, from_name, from_addr, reply_to, subject, date, auth, links, link_results, score, action, reasons, attachments, has_attachments, attachment_alert, ts (ISO with offset), dry_run, executed:false. Add the id to state.processed and update last_scan.

## Scan loop (routine, every scan_interval_minutes; default 15, 30 or 45 saves usage)
1. Fetch new inbox messages into raw/.
2. Run `python3 scan.py` (use `--dry-run` for reports only; it takes no actions).
3. For each line with executed:false, take the action (spam/report, or review label/folder), set executed:true, and alert the user for every spam or review action.
4. For every attachment_alert, regardless of score, alert: "⚠️ Attachment(s) could not be scanned — verify they are safe before opening". Include the attachments, sender, reply-to, subject, date, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, link results, score, reasons, and action taken.
5. First catch (once only): after the first ever spam or review action, if state.thanks_sent isn't true, also send exactly: "That's Inbox Guardian's first catch 🛡️ Enjoying it? You can [share it on X](https://x.com/intent/post?text=Inbox%20Guardian%20just%20caught%20a%20scam%20email%20in%20my%20inbox%20%F0%9F%9B%A1%EF%B8%8F%20Free%20Grok%20Bot%20template%20by%20%40nft_dreww) or tip NFT_Dreww on X Money as a thanks!" Then set thanks_sent:true and never send it again.
6. Send alerts per config: Grok Bot chat message, email (to alert_email from the bot's inbox or the user's account), or both.
7. Delete raw files older than 7 days.

## HTML dashboard (make_dashboard.py → dashboard.html, self-contained)
- Dark page with a CSS animation: a bot with a scan beam over a conveyor belt of envelopes.
- Envelope colors: green when clean; yellow when the log has flagged emails; red, dropping off the belt, ONLY if at least one email in the log was blocked. No red anywhere otherwise.
- Stat cards: Scanned, Clean, Blocked, Flagged, auth failures, 📎 Attachment alerts.
- Top 8 reasons (prefix before ":"), and a table of the last 25 actions (time, action, score, from, subject with 📎 if it has attachments, reasons).
- Escape all email text before writing it into the HTML.
- Refresh at the configured times. html: tell the user the file path on the box. netlify: deploy only the single file. Warn that each deploy uses Netlify build/deploy credits; keep the cadence low (twice a day) and never deploy on every scan.
- Every reason in Top reasons and Recent actions gets a plain-English explanation a normal user understands (what it means and why it matters).
- Uptime section with friendly component names and a plain-English incidents table (Time, What, What happened, Status, Do I need to do anything?). Raw errors only in a tooltip.

## In-chat dashboard (no HTML, nothing external)
When config.dashboard includes "chat", or whenever the owner asks for the dashboard in chat, compute stats from log.jsonl, state.json, health.jsonl, and breach.json and post one chat message in Markdown (never invent numbers):
- Title line: "🛡️ Inbox Guardian dashboard, <date> at <time> <tz>".
- **Since last refresh** table: Scanned | Clean | Flagged for review | Blocked | Attachments.
- **All time (since <first scan date>)** table: the same columns.
- **Every catch so far** table (blocked and flagged only, newest last): Date | Sender (in a code span) | Subject | Score | What I did ("Moved to spam" or "Flagged for review").
- **Scanner health** table: Part | Status, with ✅/⏸️/❌ and a plain-English note: mail connection, scans on schedule (last run time), each threat list, domain-age lookups, breach check (last result and date).
Keep subjects short; no files or links to external dashboards. If nothing was scanned since the last refresh, send nothing.

## Health check (routine, every 30 min)
healthcheck.py checks the mail connector (a cheap read such as listing labels), each feed (fresh, non-empty; URLhaus shows "skipped" with no key), RDAP lookups, state/log files, that the last scan is no older than scan_interval_minutes plus 30, and that scan.py and make_dashboard.py run. `--help` must only print usage, never run a check. Append one row to health.jsonl and compare with the previous row: alert the owner only when a component newly fails or recovers, in plain English with what it affects and what to do. Stay silent when nothing changed.

## Breach exposure check (optional, weekly)
- Get the connected address from the mail connector (e.g. the To field of an inbox message).
- breachcheck.py: GET `https://api.xposedornot.com/v1/breach-analytics?email=<urlencoded>` (free, no key; 404 or null means none found). Write breach.json: {email_masked (first 2 chars + *** + last char @domain), checked_at, source:"XposedOrNot", breach_count, breaches:[{name, date (xposed_date), domain, data_classes (split xposed_data on ";"), password_risk}], password_exposed (any data class mentions passwords, or password_risk is known), pastes}. Never store or display passwords or the full email.
- Dashboard "Breach exposure" panel: masked email, breach count, password exposed yes/no, breach list (name, date, data exposed), last checked, reminders (unique passwords via a password manager, change every 6 months, keep 2FA on), and the disclaimer: "⚠️ Best effort, not 100%. Breach data may be incomplete or delayed. Check pentester.com for the latest real-time results and follow good security practices."
- Weekly routine (only if the user opted in): keep the previous breach.json, re-run the check, and alert the user ONLY about breach names that weren't there before. For each new breach, include its name, date, data exposed, and what to do (change the affected passwords, enable 2FA). Refresh the dashboard.
- pentester.com has no API, and its robots.txt says "No automated tools please". Never automate it, scrape it, or bypass a captcha there; only point the user to it.

## 24h pentester reminder (one-time)
When setup completes, create a one-time routine for 24 hours later. When it fires, message the user: "Please check your email for data breaches and info-stealer leaks at https://pentester.com/checker. If anything shows up: change the affected passwords, turn on 2FA, and keep rotating passwords every 6 months." Then delete that routine.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: Run on first conversation with a new owner of this scam-scanner bot (or when they say "set me up"/"start over") to collect preferences one question at a time and launch the scanner.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Run on first conversation with a new owner of this scam-scanner bot (or when
  they say "set me up"/"start over") to collect preferences one question at a
  time and launch the scanner.
---
# Getting started (onboarding a new owner)

Greet the owner briefly: this bot watches their inbox for phishing and scam emails, moves high-confidence scams to spam, flags suspicious ones for review, and alerts them in real time. Email content is only analyzed on the bot's own computer. Ask ONE question per message, wait for the answer, and offer a default where one exists.

1. Which email provider: Gmail, Outlook, or Proton Mail?
2. Connect it.
   - Gmail or Outlook: use InstallPlugin for that provider (or AuthenticateMcpServer if it's already installed) and wait until it's connected.
   - Proton: explain that it needs a paid plan plus Proton Mail Bridge running on the box. Walk them through installing and signing in to Bridge, then ask for the Bridge IMAP username and password. Store these as a secret, never in memory text.
3. Scan the last 200 emails first as a dry-run report (no actions), then watch new mail? Alternatively, new mail only.
4. How often should I scan for new mail? Default every 15 minutes; every 30 or 45 minutes uses less of their Grok Bot usage.
5. How do you want your dashboard? Options:
   - **In-chat dashboard** (default, no files, nothing hosted outside): a summary posted right in chat with tables for since last refresh, all time, every catch, and scanner health.
   - **Local HTML file**: an animated page saved on the bot's computer and attached in chat.
   - **Hosted on Netlify**: a web link (each update uses Netlify credits).
   They can pick more than one, and can ask for any format at any time ("show my dashboard in chat").
6. How often should the dashboard be sent? Default 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM.
7. Alerts: email, Grok Bot app chat, or both? If email, which address?
8. Auto-block threshold: emails scoring above this go to spam and are reported. Default 90 (range 70–99).
9. Flagged (suspicious but below the threshold) emails: apply a label, or move them to a "Scam Review" folder?
10. What's your timezone?
11. Want weekly data-breach checks for your email? (yes/no)
12. Which attachments should trigger an "unscanned attachment" alert: all, only from unknown senders, or only risky file types?
13. Optional: add a free abuse.ch Auth-Key (from https://auth.abuse.ch/) to turn on the URLhaus malicious-link list? Ask for it with a secret request, never in chat. Without it, the other lists still work.

Before going live, show this disclaimer and get an OK: "⚠️ Inbox Guardian is a best-effort helper, not a guarantee. It can miss scams or flag safe mail, so stay careful with links, attachments, and requests for money or passwords."

Then:
- Save the answers to memory (no secrets) and write `~/scam-scanner/config.json` (dashboard: "chat", "html", "netlify", or a list; scan_interval_minutes from question 4).
- Build the scanner by following @scam-email-scanner. Verify that feeds download and that one message parses.
- If they chose the backfill: fetch the last 200 inbox messages, run `scan.py --dry-run`, and give a summary (counts, top reasons, anything above the review threshold). Ask before going live. Mark those ids processed so they aren't actioned later, unless the owner wants them actioned.
- Create routines in the owner's timezone:
  - "Scam scan": at the chosen interval, run the @scam-email-scanner scan loop.
  - "Scam dashboard": at the chosen times, send the dashboard in each chosen format (in-chat summary, attached HTML file, and/or Netlify deploy).
  - "Scam scanner health check": every 30 minutes, run the @scam-email-scanner health check and alert only when something breaks or recovers.
  - If they said yes to breach checks: run the @scam-email-scanner breach check once now and report the results (breach names, dates, data exposed; never passwords). Then create a "Breach check" routine that runs weekly and alerts only on new breaches.
  - Always: create the one-time "pentester reminder" routine for 24h after setup (see @scam-email-scanner). It deletes itself after sending.
- Confirm the setup with a short recap: provider, scan interval, threshold, flag mode, alert channel, dashboard format and times, breach checks on/off, and the 24h reminder.

routines.name: Scam email scan
routines.description: Fires on the scan interval to check new inbox mail for scams, act on them, and alert the owner.
routines.content:
Scan new inbox emails for scams using the setup in ~/scam-scanner/ and the scam-email-scanner skill. Only new INBOX messages not already in state.json; never touch spam, junk, or trash. Fetch each new message in raw form (for SPF/DKIM/DMARC headers), save to raw/, run scan.py (live, not dry-run). Above the block threshold: mark the message as spam (this moves and reports it). Suspicious but at or below the threshold: apply the 'Scam Review' label or folder (create it once if missing). Log every action to log.jsonl. Whenever an action is taken (spam or flag), alert the owner with sender, subject, score, top reasons, and action taken. Also, for every new email with an attachment that matches the attachment-alert setting, alert the owner that the attachment can't be scanned and they must make sure it's safe before opening, and include the attachment names, types, and sizes, the sender, reply-to, subject, date, SPF/DKIM/DMARC results, link check results, score, reasons, and any action taken. If nothing new, everything is clean, and there are no attachments, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `@every 45m`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Scam dashboard refresh
routines.description: Fires at the owner's chosen dashboard times to send a summary of what the scanner caught.
routines.content:
Build the scam-scanner dashboard in each format the owner chose in config.json (default: in-chat markdown tables only, with nothing published to an external site). Read ~/scam-scanner/log.jsonl and the latest entry of health.jsonl. For the in-chat format, send a short title line, then tables for: Since last refresh (Scanned, Clean, Flagged for review, Blocked, Attachments), All time (same columns), Every catch so far (Date, Sender, Subject, Score, What I did), and Scanner health (Part, Status), plus one plain sentence on anything worth a look. Never invent numbers. If no emails were scanned since the last refresh, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 0 9,17 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Scam scanner health check
routines.description: Fires every 30 minutes to confirm the scanner and mail connection still work, alerting only when something breaks or recovers.
routines.content:
Check that the scam scanner in ~/scam-scanner/ is working. First make a lightweight read call to the mail connector (for example, listing labels) to confirm it's connected. Then run healthcheck.py, passing --gmail ok or --gmail fail for the connector result, which logs to health.jsonl. Alert the owner only when a component newly fails or recovers compared with the previous check: say what's broken, since when, and the likely fix. If the mail connector needs re-auth, start reconnecting it. If everything is still healthy, send nothing. This runs around the clock because the scanner does too.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 13,43 * * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Weekly breach check
routines.description: Fires weekly, if the owner opted in, to alert them only about new data breaches involving their email.
routines.content:
Run the weekly breach exposure check from the scam-email-scanner skill for the connected email address: copy ~/scam-scanner/breach.json to breach.prev.json, run `python3 ~/scam-scanner/breachcheck.py <address>`, then refresh the dashboard data. Compare the results with breach.prev.json. If any breach names are new, alert the owner with each new breach's name, date, and the data exposed, and tell them to change the affected passwords and turn on 2FA. Never show passwords or the full email address. If nothing is new, stay quiet.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 17 9 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
